notes: L3 not measured: a tool format's L3 is xref_precision and xref_recall (design section 1.2), which lang-oracle computes only for a doc-engine extractor (fusion.ResolveDocXrefs), and import_resolution only for kind language, so a tags-engine tool format's imports and file-resolved edges are not scored; the oracle file already carries protoc's in-repo imports and cross-file references for the harness that scores them

cross-checks, unscored: buf build 1.70.0 (the repository's buf.yaml workspace, offline, decoded by the same program with -image) writes the same 919 definitions, 287 references, 42 imports and 11 cross-file references as protoc on the 37 files its workspace holds; universal-ctags 6.2.1 (Protobuf, tier B) matches 1,188 of the 1,192 definitions both ways (sym_recall and sym_precision .9966)
grpc/grpc-go: 22 tool-oracle entries on files fathom does not read (ingest's gates, discovery's exclusions) were left out of scope (§1.4)

import strategy file-symbol (a path under the repository root), measured outside the harness with fusion.ResolveImportSpecs against protoc's own resolution: grpc/grpc-go 3 of 3 in-repo imports, bufbuild/protovalidate 0 of 123 (its imports are rooted at buf.yaml's module paths, proto/protovalidate and proto/protovalidate-testing, which no existing strategy reads: needs-strategy)

lang-parity against protoextract.go (both subjects, protovalidate unrestricted): sym_recall .9967 to 1, sym_precision .9363 to .9696, ref_recall 0 to 1, level_met none to L2; verdict REFUSED because the target (L3) is not met, so the incumbent stays dispatched (design section 11 step 2) and the dialect is built beside it

oracle: protoc (libprotoc 34.1, tier A, the format's reference compiler) compiles each file with --include_source_info through calibration/oracles/protoc-descriptors, under the subject's buf module roots and the repository root; definitions are messages (nested ones and proto2 groups; the synthetic map-entry messages are not written), enums, services and rpcs at their source_code_info spans; references are (enclosing message or rpc, type) for every message- or enum-typed field, map value, oneof member and extension field declared in a message, and an rpc's request and response
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
range, not gated for a tool format: every matched definition's end line equals protoc's span end (1,192 of 1,192); every rpc and message carries a Signature

the incumbent's rpc Signature is the request and response type names joined by an arrow, text no source spells; a tags-engine Signature is the definition's own source up to its body (design section 3.3), so the dialect's is the rpc as written (rpc SayHello (HelloRequest) returns (HelloResponse)) and protoextract_test.go's signature case holds for the incumbent only (TestProtobufDialectRPCSignature)
disposition: partial: target L3, met L2 (L1 excellent, L2 excellent) on grpc/grpc-go v1.84.0 (10 files) and bufbuild/protovalidate v1.2.2 (118 files): sym_recall 1 and sym_precision 1 (1,192 definitions), ref_recall 1 and ref_precision 1 (456 pairs) against protoc 34.1 (tier A), 8.44 MB/CPU-s, 0 faults, 287 peak module pages, protobuf.wasm.gz 68,444 bytes. L3 is not measured: the harness scores a tool format's cross-file references only for a doc-engine extractor, and the import strategy that fits through manifest parameters (file-symbol at the repository root) resolves 3 of 126 in-repo imports, since a buf workspace roots its imports at buf.yaml's module paths (needs-strategy). The dialect is not dispatched: lang-parity refuses the port while L3 is unmet, and the incumbent's arrow-joined rpc Signature is not a source span (LB-Q-protobuf-rest)
